<!--
Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!

If you are proposing a fix for a security issue, STOP and follow .github/SECURITY.md instead.

Keep the entire pull request self-contained, reviewer-facing, and diegetic: describe the
change, rationale, and evidence within the context of the repository and pull request. Do not
narrate how the pull request was produced or refer to private conversations, prior agent work,
or other behind-the-scenes context. Omit those details unless they materially affect review;
if they do, state the relevant fact and its significance directly.
-->

<!-- List related issues here. Use `fixes` or `closes` keywords to associate an issue number. -->

Layer 11 of 11 in the stack tracked by #15070.


### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

Agents asked to wait for the CI of a pull request tend to poll `gh run watch` or `gh run view` until the workflow runs finish. The event subscriptions API now sends `com.github.pull_request.check_suite.status.changed.v1` when a check suite on the head commit of a pull request completes, with its `data.conclusion` (for example `success` or `failure`). A check suite is the group of checks from one source, such as one workflow run.

This change makes that event available in `gh event listen` and points agents at it:

- `gh event listen` accepts the new event type, lists it in its help and shell completion, and has an example that waits for the next check suite and prints its conclusion. The help explains that a pull request usually has several check suites, each sending its own event, so waiting for all checks means reading them after each event.
- When an agent runs `gh run view` or `gh run watch` on a workflow run that is not completed and belongs to a github.com pull request, the command prints a hint on stderr with the full `gh event listen` command for that pull request. It follows the existing hint printed by `gh pr view` and other pull request commands, with notes adapted to checks: read them with `gh pr checks` after each event, and run the listener again while any are pending. `gh run watch` prints it before it starts watching, so it is visible even if the watch is stopped. `gh run view` prints it with `--json` too, but not with `--web` or `--log`.
- The `gh run view` and `gh run watch` help texts gain a paragraph saying that, to wait for the workflow runs of a github.com pull request, `gh event listen` with this event is the alternative to polling.
- The `gh` agent skill and `docs/event-listen-preview.md` describe the new event and the run hints.

To share the hint layout, `PrintListenHint` in `pkg/cmd/event/shared/hint.go` now uses a private helper; its output is unchanged.


### How did you test this change?

<!--
Report only actions you actually performed and results you actually observed, using factual
first-person language (for example, "I ran..." and "I saw..."). Do not present planned,
hypothetical, inferred, or merely expected scenarios as testing.

Automated test results do not belong here. Passing unit tests, `go test ./...` output, and
coverage numbers tell a reviewer nothing they cannot see from CI, so do not paste them.

If you did not exercise the changed behavior, write `Not tested` and explain why.

Use one or more of these, whichever communicates best:

1. Screenshots or GIFs of the real command running. Preferred whenever the change is visible
   in terminal output. If output changed, show it before and after.
2. Given/When/Then scenarios, but only when you actually executed the steps. For example:
   Given I was in a repo with no open pull requests
   When I ran `gh pr list`
   Then I saw "no open pull requests in cli/cli"
3. A natural language walkthrough of what you did by hand, the states you covered, and what
   you saw, including error and edge cases.

If you leave this empty, your pull request will very likely be closed.
-->

I built `gh` from this branch and recorded the session below against babakks/cli#17, a pull request in a test repository, setting `COPILOT_CLI=1` where the agent hints were exercised.

1. When I ran `gh run view --help` and `gh run watch --help`, I saw the new paragraphs pointing at `gh event listen` and `com.github.pull_request.check_suite.status.changed.v1`.
2. Given I had dispatched the `govulncheck.yml` workflow on the pull request branch, when I ran `gh run view <run>` with `COPILOT_CLI=1` while the run was in progress, I saw the hint with `gh event listen --resource https://github.com/babakks/cli/pull/17 --event com.github.pull_request.check_suite.status.changed.v1`, followed by the usual run summary.
3. When I ran `gh run watch <run>` with `COPILOT_CLI=1`, I saw the same hint before the watch started, and it was still on screen after I stopped the watch with Ctrl-C.
4. Given I had dispatched the workflow again and the earlier run had completed, when I ran `gh event listen --resource <pr> --event com.github.pull_request.check_suite.status.changed.v1 --jq .data.conclusion`, I saw `failure` once the run completed, and the command exited after that first event. `gh run view <run> --json conclusion` then reported `failure` for the dispatched run.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77bea7f9-8760-49e7-9d71-268b7c1d2182


### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

- The hint names the pull request, not the run, because check suite events are subscribed per pull request. A run that does not belong to a pull request gets no hint.
- The hint suggests the default one-shot listener and leaves `--count` and `--follow` out. The number of check suites per pull request is not known in advance, so reading the checks after each event and listening again is more reliable than a fixed count.
- Completed runs get no hint, since there is nothing left to wait for.


### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Link related issues or prior discussion, with one sentence on why each matters.
-->

Start with `PrintChecksListenHint` in `pkg/cmd/event/shared/hint.go`, then the call sites in `pkg/cmd/run/view/hint.go`, `pkg/cmd/run/view/view.go`, and `pkg/cmd/run/watch/watch.go`, and their tests. The first commit adds the event type to `gh event listen`; the second adds the run hints and help text.


### Authorship and follow-up

<!--
REQUIRED - If you are an AI agent filling in this template, answer "Who wrote this" for yourself and answer honestly. For "Who answers review comments," use only a choice the human has explicitly made in the conversation. If no choice has already been established, pause and ask the human to choose one of the three options before creating or updating the pull request. Do not infer the choice from repository ownership, authorship, assignees, prior interactions, or the current operator. After the human answers, check exactly the option they chose; the last option is valid when the human explicitly chooses nobody.

Check exactly one box in each list.
-->

Who wrote this:

- [ ] A human wrote it.
- [x] An agent wrote it under close human direction.
- [ ] An agent wrote it independently, and no human has guided the implementation beyond the initial prompt.

Who answers review comments:

- [x] @babakks will read and reply directly. Name the account.
- [ ] An agent will draft replies and @babakks will read them before they are posted.
- [ ] Nobody has explicitly committed to replying.

### 🟡 Changes recommended Pending commit statuses can cause indefinite waits, and branch-only matching can suggest events for an outdated PR; required test coverage is also missing.
6 open issues - [Exclude pending commit statuses from the listener wait](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15081#discussion_r4603268588) · New - [Verify the run is associated with the current PR head](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15081#discussion_r4603268686) · New - [Test completion for the check-suite event type](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15081#discussion_r4603268785) · New - [Test JSON hint suppression on lookup failure and unsupported hosts](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15081#discussion_r4603268918) · New - [Test agent hint suppression for negative cases](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15081#discussion_r4603269018) · New - [Use require.NoError for the watch error check](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15081#discussion_r4603269110) · New
What changed in this PR Completes the event-streaming stack tracked in #15070 by exposing check-suite completion events and helping agents discover event-driven waiting for pull request CI on github.com. **Changes:** - Adds the check-suite event to event help, shell completion, and listener examples. - Adds agent-only hints to unfinished `gh run view` and `gh run watch` invocations, sharing the existing hint layout. - Updates run help, tests, agent guidance, and preview documentation. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `skills/​gh/​SKILL.md` | Documents event-driven CI waiting and checking remaining suites. | | `pkg/​cmd/​run/​watch/​watch.go` | Adds agent detection, waiting guidance, and a pre-watch hint. | | `pkg/​cmd/​run/​watch/​watch_test.go` | Tests hint output for agent and human callers. | | `pkg/​cmd/​run/​view/​view.go` | Adds waiting guidance and hints for regular and JSON output paths. | | `pkg/​cmd/​run/​view/​view_test.go` | Tests hints across run states, caller types, and JSON output. | | `pkg/​cmd/​run/​view/​hint.go` | Centralizes view-specific hint eligibility and printing. | | `pkg/​cmd/​event/​shared/​hint.go` | Shares hint formatting and adds check-suite waiting advice. | | `pkg/​cmd/​event/​shared/​help.go` | Adds the check-suite event name and description. | | `pkg/​cmd/​event/​shared/​completion_test.go` | Updates the unknown-event completion fixture. | | `pkg/​cmd/​event/​listen/​listen.go` | Explains check-suite events and adds a conclusion-printing example. | | `docs/​event-listen-preview.md` | Documents check-suite payloads and run-command hints. |
Review effort: Balanced

🛑 Requirement: Handle pending commit statuses separately

`gh pr checks` includes commit status contexts, whose completion does not emit a check-suite event, so an agent can wait indefinitely when only those remain pending. Limit the listener loop to check-suite-backed checks and provide a fallback such as `gh pr checks --watch` for pending statuses. Apply the same qualification in `skills/gh/SKILL.md:325`, `pkg/cmd/event/listen/listen.go:99-101`, and `docs/event-listen-preview.md:22,44`.

🛑 Requirement: Verify the run belongs to the suggested PR

The lookup matches only the branch and repository, so reusing a branch after its PR was merged can produce a hint for that old PR's checks and events. Verify the run's association with a current PR and the head covered by these events before offering the listener, rather than relying on branch-name equality. Same issue in `pkg/cmd/run/watch/watch.go:165`.

🛑 Requirement: Test completion of the new event type

The completion test only changes an unknown-prefix case; none of its positive cases exercises this new type. Add a case for the check-suite prefix and its full suggestion so the advertised shell completion is covered.

🛑 Requirement: Cover failed lookup and unsupported-host JSON paths

The new JSON test covers only an in-progress run with a matching github.com PR. Please also exercise a missing or failed PR lookup and a non-github.com repository, asserting that JSON still succeeds without a hint; these are important suppression and error-handling paths added before the exporter.

🛑 Requirement: Cover the hint's negative cases for agent callers

The new watch tests only exercise a matching github.com PR; the existing completed-run tests do not set an agent. Please add agent cases for a completed run, no matching PR, and an unsupported host, asserting that stderr has no event hint. These are explicit conditions of the new behavior.

🛑 Requirement: Stop the test when the watch fails

`docs/testing.md` requires `require` for error checks so dependent assertions do not run after an unexpected error. Please use `require.NoError` here and add its import.
